text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Finland alone to propose that the European Union's (EU) crisis management would be handled by the Western European Union (WEU), and negotiators in inter-governmental conference had to yield to that military intervention be the EU's responsibility.
- State asset management company Arsenal has offered the Seurahuone hotel and banking building near parliament as an alternative to the legislature's plans for a new building.
- Pain-killers too scarcely used in Finland, anaesthesia doctors say.
- Finns spend an average of 3,500 markka per year on their looks. Urban under 25-year-olds biggest spenders, almost 4,200 markka per year.
- DNA-testing of Somalis seeking to join their families in Finland reversed some 120 refusals to enter the country, but the method will not be used regularly due to high costs, officials say.
- Most antennaes must be improved for reception of the new commercial national television channel Neloskanava.

- Neste personnel appealing to Minister of Trade and Industry Antti Kalliomaki to stop Neste's plans to sell its 50 percent stake in polyolefins group Borealis and the polystyrene operation which concerns some 1,300 employees.

- The Aland island administration is planning local voting right for all people who have lived there for three years, which has previously been reserved for people registered as Aland citizens in violation of EU rules.

- Japanese newspaper Nikkan Kogyo Shimbu says NTT Docomo has chosen Nokia for cooperation to develop the next generation of Japanese mobile phones, but Nokia is not among those to develop new infrastructure. Swedish Rival Ericsson is.
KAUPPALEHTI
- PK Cables' management share of the company's initial public offering is 60.5 million markka, most of which is pure profit.
- Kone CEO Anssi Soila declines to comment whether Kone may get a chance to buy parts of German rival Thyssen if Krupp, which holds 10 percent of votes in Kone, succeeds in its Thyssen takeover bid.

- Forest industry production is expanding and globalising and there will be an increasing number of alternative locations for future plants, says professor Matti Palo at the Finnish Forest Research Institute (METLA).
AAMULEHTI
- Finland's forest industry is facing a growing challenge from cultivated forests in southern countries and needs diversification and product development, says METLA professor Matti Palo.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Tapani Kahri, deputy managing director at the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT), proposes a two-layer incomes settlement, with pay agreements for one to two years and other details agreed for five to seven years.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Pop-star Michael Jackson to give his first concert in Finland at the Olympic Stadium in Helsinki on August 24. The concert is part of Jackson's HIStory world tour.
- Ordinary flight passengers to and from Finland are in for delays during the next couple of days due to the U.S.-Russia summit.
